questions.question: A closed system is one that exchanges with its surroundings:
Chemical equilibrium is the state of a reversible reaction in a closed system in which:
options: The forward and reverse rates are equal, so concentrations remain constant
The concentrations of reactants and products are equal
All the reactants have been converted to products

questions.question: The equilibrium is called DYNAMIC because:
options: Both reactions continue at particle level while the totals stay constant
The system responds violently to disturbances

questions.question: Equilibrium cannot establish itself in an open system because:
options: The forward reaction is too slow
Catalysts do not work in open systems
Escaping products starve the reverse reaction of its ingredients

questions.question: Le Chatelier's principle states that a disturbed equilibrium will:
options: Favour the reaction that opposes the disturbance, establishing a new equilibrium
Return exactly to its original state
Stop reacting until the disturbance is removed

questions.question: For 2SO₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2SO₃ (forward exothermic), RAISING the temperature will:
options: Shift the equilibrium toward SO₂ and O₂, lowering the yield

questions.question: For the same reaction (3 gas moles left, 2 right), INCREASING the pressure will:
options: Have no effect on the position
Shift toward SO₃ — the side with fewer gas moles

questions.question: Adding a catalyst to an equilibrium mixture:
options: Shifts the equilibrium toward the products
Speeds both directions equally — equilibrium is reached sooner with the same yield

questions.question: On a concentration-time graph, a vertical jump in ONE species' line indicates:
options: That species was suddenly added or removed at that instant

questions.question: ALL gaseous concentration lines jumping at the same instant signals:
options: A change in the vessel's volume (pressure change)

questions.question: A temperature change shows on a concentration-time graph as:
options: No jump at all — only curves bending toward new levels

questions.question: On a rate-time graph, adding a catalyst appears as:
options: The forward rate spiking while the reverse decays
Both rate lines jumping upward together and meeting sooner

questions.question: In the Kc expression, pure solids and pure liquids are:
options: Left out entirely — their concentrations are constant
Written with an exponent of one

questions.question: H₂ + I₂ ⇌ 2HI in a 4 dm³ vessel: 2,0 mol of each reactant injected; 3,0 mol HI at equilibrium. The equilibrium concentration of H₂ is:
With [HI] = 0,75 and [H₂] = [I₂] = 0,125 mol·dm⁻³, Kc for this reaction equals:
The ONLY change that alters the value of Kc is:

subtopics.title: The Shop Where the Crowd Never Changes

questions.question: In the shop picture, the constant crowd of 150 with thirty entering and thirty leaving each minute represents:
options: Dynamic equilibrium — constant concentrations with two-way traffic continuing

questions.question: The shop analogy shows that 'constant' concentrations at equilibrium:
options: Must be equal for reactants and products
Need not be equal — the steady crowd can be large or small

questions.question: The 'missing back wall' through which shoppers drift away and never return represents:
options: An open system, in which equilibrium cannot establish

questions.question: The see-saw picture captures the key feature of every equilibrium response: the disturbance is:
For an exothermic forward reaction, the trick of 'writing heat into the equation' places heat:
Squeezing a gaseous equilibrium into a smaller volume sends it toward:
options: The side with more gas moles
The side with fewer gas moles — relieving the crowding

questions.question: In the see-saw picture the catalyst 'greases the pivot', meaning it:
options: Tilts the see-saw toward the products
Removes weight from the reactant seat
Brings balance sooner without changing the final tilt

questions.question: A Kc value in the thousands tells you the equilibrium mixture is:
options: Nearly all products — the forward reaction almost went to completion
An equal mix of reactants and products

questions.question: The four-line bookkeeping for a Kc calculation runs:
options: In, change, remain, then divide by the volume

questions.question: The most expensive shortcut in a Kc calculation is:
options: Substituting raw moles instead of dividing by the vessel's volume first

questions.question: Adding reactant, changing pressure and adding catalyst all leave Kc unchanged because:
options: Kc is not affected by concentrations at all
The concentrations rearrange until the same ratio is restored — only temperature rewrites the score
